from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
path = 'src/data/lyrics/tanha-hun-dasht-e-bala-mein-abbas-kahan-ho.md'
before = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + path], text=True)
after = Path(path).read_text()
_, metadata, body = after.split('---', 2)
roman = metadata.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1]
def verses(block):
    return [line.strip() for line in block.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit()]
assert [line.casefold() for line in verses(roman)] == [line.casefold() for line in verses(before.split('---', 2)[2])]
assert [len(verses(block)) for block in roman.strip().replace('  \\n', '\\n').split('\\n\\n')] == [len(verses(block)) for block in body.strip().split('\\n\\n')] == [4] + [3] * 8
print('Verified all 28 Roman verses and matching Urdu stanza lengths.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 28 verses in Urdu script and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`, with capitalization normalized. Both editions have a four-line opening and eight matching stanzas. Updated the title and right-to-left direction and removed the `noUrdu` tag.

I read the ambiguous Roman word `kahara` as `قہراً` and retained the original Roman spelling.
